title: Jaiswal and Rahul's 130-Run Stand Blunts New Zealand's Advantage in Wellington
excerpt: India reached 159 for 1 at stumps on Day 2 of the first Test, trailing New Zealand's 368 by 209 runs, after Yashasvi Jaiswal's 85 and KL Rahul's unbeaten 52 produced India's first century opening stand in 17 Tests.
body:
• India closed Day 2 of the first Test at 159 for 1 in 39 overs, trailing New Zealand's 368 by 209 runs at the Basin Reserve in Wellington.
  • Yashasvi Jaiswal (85 off 89 balls) and KL Rahul (52 not out) added 130 for the first wicket — India's first century opening stand in 17 Tests, and its first on New Zealand soil in 32 years.
  • Henry Nicholls' unbeaten 175 and Glenn Phillips' 118 carried New Zealand from 243 for 5 overnight to 368 all out; Jasprit Bumrah took 4 for 92 and Akash Deep 3 for 53.
  • Rahul resumes on Day 3 with Devdutt Padikkal, who is 16 not out, with India holding nine wickets in hand.

India's openers gave their side the reply it needed on Day 2 of the first Test in Wellington. After Henry Nicholls' unbeaten 175 lifted New Zealand to 368, Yashasvi Jaiswal and KL Rahul put on 130 for the first wicket — India's first century opening stand in 17 Tests — and took the visitors to 159 for 1 at stumps, 209 runs behind with nine wickets standing.

Nicholls and Phillips stretch New Zealand to 368

"Nicholls was left unbeaten on 175 off 335 balls, with 21 boundaries."

New Zealand resumed at 243 for 5, already rescued from 70 for 5 on the opening day, and Nicholls and Glenn Phillips extended their sixth-wicket partnership to 216 — New Zealand's second-highest stand for the sixth wicket or lower against India, behind only Brendon McCullum and BJ Watling's 352 at the same ground in 2014. Phillips made 118 off 216 balls, his second Test century, and became the first New Zealand batter to score centuries against the same opposition in all three formats. Akash Deep finally broke the stand, beating Phillips' off stump, and after lunch the innings folded quickly: Prasidh Krishna trapped Nathan Smith lbw, Kyle Jamieson gloved an Akash Deep short ball to slip, Bumrah trapped Matt Henry in front for his fourth wicket, and Anshul Kamboj dismissed Jacob Duffy to end the innings. Nicholls was left unbeaten on 175 off 335 balls, with 21 boundaries. Bumrah finished with 4 for 92 and Akash Deep 3 for 53, and New Zealand's last five wickets fell for 82 runs.

India's openers answer

The reply began in survival mode. New Zealand opened with four successive maidens, Rahul survived a review in a Kyle Jamieson over and was fortunate that New Zealand did not review a Matt Henry lbw shout that replays showed would have been three reds; Jaiswal edged through the slips and was missed by Phillips at gully. India reached tea at 16 without loss. The final session was a different game: the pair added 81 runs in the first 15 overs after tea, Jaiswal reaching a 66-ball fifty and bringing up the century partnership with a ramp shot — India's first hundred opening stand since the same pair's 201 in Perth in November 2024, and its first in New Zealand since Nayan Mongia and Navjot Sidhu's 102 in Hamilton in 1994. At 130, it is also India's second-highest opening partnership in New Zealand, behind Manoj Prabhakar and WV Raman's 149 in Auckland in 1990, according to Nation Press.

The stand ended when Jaiswal, on 85 off 89 balls with 16 fours, nicked Henry to wicketkeeper Tom Blundell standing up to the stumps, New Zealand getting the decision on review. Rahul played the anchor's innings: his unbeaten 52 off 116 balls was his 22nd Test fifty, his first against New Zealand, and it means he now has fifty-plus scores in all four SENA countries — South Africa, England, New Zealand and Australia. Devdutt Padikkal survived a watchful start to reach 16 not out at the close.

Where the match stands

Brief scores: New Zealand 368 (Henry Nicholls 175 not out, Glenn Phillips 118; Jasprit Bumrah 4 for 92, Akash Deep 3 for 53) lead India 159 for 1 (Yashasvi Jaiswal 85, KL Rahul 52 not out; Matt Henry 1 for 43) by 209 runs. Day 3 begins on Saturday with Rahul and Padikkal at the crease; India's first task is to erase the remaining deficit, and the size of any first-innings lead will shape the rest of this Test.
